experiments.hypothesis: The medium-tier run suggested cheaper crews hold quality with review, CI and auto-fix behind them. On hard tasks, give one arm per model (sonnet, grok, terra, muse-wonder) against the live hard pool. That shows which models can carry hard work at lower cost without raising rework, recoveries or escapes. Control reads the live pool, unpinned, by Daniel's choice.
experiments.name: hard-tier-by-model

experiments.hypothesis: The 2026-10-27 riskiness backtests found escaped regressions per line changed about equal across crews (per-file spread ~0.8–1.27x, within noise). Either crews are over-qualified for medium work, or the review gate, CI and auto-fix absorb the capability gap at a cost. Randomly assigning medium tasks to the cheap pool (luna, haiku, muse-spark) instead of the current medium pool (sol, muse-wonder) separates the two. If the treatment cuts cost with no rise in rework, recoveries or escapes, medium work is over-staffed. If it matches on escapes but costs more in review repairs and recoveries, the pipeline is paying for the gap.
experiments.name: medium-tier-cheap-crews
